crossroads.kicker: Story Crossroads • Tuesday, August 21, 2001, 9:50 AM — 1961 Norfolk Pathfinder Terminal
crossroads.title: Inside the Monticello Locker Alcove: Does Nolan Reject Tammy Now or Wait While She Buys Tickets?
crossroads.prompt: Wheeled six feet behind the thick concrete column into the recessed steel coin-locker alcove leading to the 1961 Monticello Avenue terminal's separate Men's and Women's restrooms—shielded from concourse security by the lockers, Tammy's back, and her open baby-blue cardigan wings—twenty-three-year-old Nolan Lennox faces Tammy's ultimate trump card: a silent two-second flash beneath her braless shelf-bra camisole and a soft Week-One promise of zero yelling in Seattle plus a payphone call to Blue Tech in Richmond. Every option opens a complete, coequal story route.

options.label: Reject Tammy's Promise & Roll Out Before She Buys Tickets
options.subtitle: Realize peaceful, yell-free hugs with Gwen beat empty promises every time—rolling straight out from behind the lockers into plain view of the waiting room to lock your wheelchair brakes, tell Tammy you're breaking up for good, and head back home to Gwen and Grandpa Walter in Emerald Creek.

options.label: Believe Tammy's Promise While She Buys the Ninety-Nine-Dollar Tickets
options.subtitle: Take Tammy's velvet Week-One promise and Richmond payphone assurance at face value—easing your hands off your wheel locks and waiting in the concourse while she walks up to the counter to buy two ninety-nine-dollar cash tickets to Seattle.

crossroads.kicker: Story Crossroads • Tuesday, August 21, 2001, 9:56 AM — Gate Four, Norfolk Pathfinder Terminal
crossroads.title: Paid Tickets and Four Steep Steps: Does Tammy Snap or Keep Her Week-One Voice?
crossroads.prompt: With two freshly printed ninety-nine-dollar Seattle ticket folders in Tammy's hand, the Gate Four driver shakes his head at Nolan's manual wheelchair: nobody called corporate forty-eight hours ahead for a hydraulic lift, meaning Nolan's chair must ride folded in the luggage bay while he climbs four steep aluminum steps on his forearm crutches. What Tammy says next decides whether Nolan steps aboard.

options.label: Tammy Snaps at Gate Four — Refuse to Board & Go Home
options.subtitle: The instant Tammy drops her sweet voice and snaps at you in front of the boarding queue, wake up to the lie, ask the driver to pull your wheelchair back out of the luggage bay, and roll straight back inside the waiting room to break up for good and go home.

options.label: Tammy Keeps Her Sweet Week-One Voice — Board the Pathfinder
options.subtitle: Reassured by Tammy's warm, patient Week-One smile—apologizing to the driver, carrying your metal footrests, and promising to call Blue Tech together in Richmond and ask the desk for a lift coach—trust her word and climb the four steep aluminum steps onto Gate Four.

crossroads.kicker: Story Crossroads • Wednesday, August 22, 2001, 8:05 PM — Emerald Creek Blue Tech
crossroads.title: Missed Shift Number One: Does Mallory Check on Nolan Tonight or Wait Until Friday?
crossroads.prompt: Eight-oh-five clicks onto the Emerald Creek Blue Tech breakroom timeclock—marking the first No-Call No-Show of Nolan Lennox's spotless two-year career. Quietly in love with Nolan yet bound both by respect for his relationship and by corporate HR's rule to wait until Friday's third missed shift before calling an emergency contact, Computers Shift Supervisor Mallory Walsh stands beside her car four blocks from Grandpa Walter's house off Eden Way North.

options.label: Drive Down Eden Way North Tonight
options.subtitle: Trust your gut over corporate HR's three-day waiting rule—driving four blocks down Eden Way North right after closing tonight to check on Nolan with Gwen and Grandpa Walter before another day slips away.

options.label: Respect Corporate Protocol & Wait Until Friday's Third No-Show
options.subtitle: Honor corporate HR rules and off-the-clock boundaries—holding back until Friday evening's third missed shift gives you official reason to call Grandpa Walter's landline.
forbidden_terms: Five Minutes Before the Restroom Door

crossroads.kicker: Story Crossroads • Second Afternoon of the Twin Moons, The Sunken Milestone
crossroads.title: Three Gentle Roads Toward the Waystation: How Do Nolan, Gwen, and Mallory Travel?
crossroads.prompt: With both wheelchairs and Mallory's sneakers left behind in Studio 205 on Earth, barefoot twenty-four-year-old Nolan Lennox, his six-foot-one nineteen-year-old sister Gwen, and his twenty-four-year-old girlfriend Mallory Walsh have learned why Vaeloria's sleeping Three-Ring Bronze Astrolabe answered their Friday-night wish: only an astronomer's eye, a truth-reader's diagnostic mind, and a guardian's unhurried heart turning together can heal The Great Drift. Here at the Sunken Milestone, peddler Bramwell Kettle shows all three of them three gentle 1980s-fantasy routes winding inward. Every option opens a complete, coequal story route.

options.label: The Glasswater Lantern-Barge Canal
options.subtitle: Step aboard barge-master Maren's wide reed-and-cedar lantern boat—cuddling three-across on cushioned planks with Nolan's and Gwen's forearm crutches stowed safe beside the gunwale while Gwen's astronomy eye, Mallory's lock-cipher logic, and Nolan's current-reading eye guide the vessel upriver.

options.label: The Whisperwood Cushion-Moss Road
options.subtitle: Walk unhurriedly three abreast at Nolan and Gwen's forearm-crutch pace over three-inch velvet moss laid by the Slow-Footed Order, soaking six bare feet in 98-degree mineral springs and curling up three-across in cozy stone shelters as your shared footsteps reawaken sleepy forest lanterns.

options.label: The Brass Counterweight Gondola Way
options.subtitle: Board the oak-and-brass water-balanced sky gondola rising smoothly into the Amber Crags past singing bronze wind-harps, helping the cliffside Star-Keepers recalibrate moon-and-vernier rings knocked out of phase by The Great Drift.
